bands.name: Palmar radiocarpal ligament
bands.mechanical_role: the wrist's strongest capsular ligament; guides the characteristic screw-home-like coupled motion during wrist extension
bands.function_note: Broad, strong palmar band; its integrity is the main reason the palmar wrist capsule is stronger than the dorsal capsule.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Dorsal radiocarpal ligament
bands.mechanical_role: secondary dorsal restraint, weaker than its palmar counterpart
bands.function_note: The thinner, weaker dorsal counterpart to the palmar radiocarpal ligament.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Ulnar collateral ligament of wrist
bands.mechanical_role: resists radial deviation stress; blends with the triangular fibrocartilage complex
bands.function_note: Functionally continuous with the TFCC (see data/cartilage/) rather than a fully separable discrete cord.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Radial collateral ligament of wrist
bands.function_note: Continues distally into the thenar region, blending with the abductor pollicis brevis fascia.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

bands.name: Scapholunate interosseous ligament
bands.mechanical_role: the primary stabilizer of the scapholunate joint; its dorsal region, described by Berger (1996) as thick with short transversely-oriented collagen fibers, is reported by separate biomechanical load-to-failure testing (not this histologic paper itself) as the mechanically strongest of its three regions -- consistent findings from two different kinds of study, not a single paper's claim (precision clarified after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md)
bands.function_note: Clinically the single most important intrinsic carpal ligament -- its rupture causes scapholunate dissociation (the classic 'Terry Thomas sign' gap on radiographs) and, if untreated, progresses to SLAC (scapholunate advanced collapse) wrist arthritis.
bands.source: Berger RA (1996) 'The gross and histologic anatomy of the scapholunate interosseous ligament.' J Hand Surg Am 21(2):170-178 -- scapholunate ligament's dorsal/palmar/proximal membranous regions and role in carpal stability.

bands.name: Lunotriquetral interosseous ligament

attachments.landmark_a: lunate (distal/ulnar pole; dorsal, palmar, and proximal-membranous regions)

bands.mechanical_role: the primary intrinsic stabilizer of the lunotriquetral joint, resisting a volar intercalated segment instability (VISI) collapse pattern; its palmar subregion -- not its dorsal subregion -- is the mechanically dominant and thickest of its three parts, the reverse of the scapholunate ligament's dorsally-dominant biomechanics
bands.function_note: The scapholunate ligament's clinical and mechanical counterpart on the ulnar side of the proximal carpal row; the two are almost always discussed together in carpal instability. Cadaveric multiaxis testing of its three subregions found the palmar subregion thickest (~2.3mm) and strongest (failure load ~301N vs ~121N dorsal and ~64N proximal) and the main restraint to palmar translation and axial rotation. Its rupture produces lunotriquetral instability/dissociation, generally a less common and less severe injury than scapholunate disruption.
bands.source: Ritt MJ, Bishop AT, Berger RA, Linscheid RL, Berglund LJ, An KN (1998) 'Lunotriquetral ligament properties: a comparison of three anatomic subregions.' J Hand Surg Am 23(3):425-431, doi:10.1016/S0363-5023(05)80460-5 -- retrieved via PubMed.

bands.name: Pisohamate ligament
bands.mechanical_role: accessory band continuing the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon's pull across the pisotriquetral joint onto the hamate
bands.function_note: One of the pisiform's two distal fibrous extensions (with the pisometacarpal ligament) that let the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon act indirectly on the hamate and fifth metacarpal, effectively making the pisiform a sesamoid pulley for FCU's line of pull; forms part of the floor of Guyon's canal.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Pisometacarpal ligament
bands.mechanical_role: accessory band continuing the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon's pull onto the base of the fifth metacarpal
bands.function_note: The second of the pisiform's two distal fibrous extensions (with the pisohamate ligament); together they are functionally the true distal insertion of flexor carpi ulnaris, since the tendon itself ends on the pisiform rather than reaching the hamate or metacarpal directly.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

function: The wrist capsule's major thickenings plus the scapholunate and lunotriquetral interosseous ligaments and the pisiform's accessory pisohamate/pisometacarpal bands, together maintaining normal carpal alignment and coupled radiocarpal/midcarpal kinematics through wrist flexion-extension and radioulnar deviation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Berger RA (1996) 'The gross and histologic anatomy of the scapholunate interosseous ligament.'
